parties: Arun Kumar Saraf; Asian Hotels (East) Limited
headline: Arun Kumar Saraf Files Substantial Acquisition Disclosure for Asian Hotels (East) Limited
sum: Arun Kumar Saraf has filed a Regulation 10(5) disclosure with NSE, signalling a substantial acquisition of shares in Asian Hotels (East) Limited, the Kolkata-based hospitality company.
implication: Substantial acquisition disclosures under Reg. 10(5) trigger mandatory general offer requirements if thresholds (25% or such trigger) are breached; careful attention to creeping acquisition exemptions and the calculation of 'in the money' convertible securities is critical.
detail: Arun Kumar Saraf, an acquirer, has submitted to NSE a disclosure under Regulation 10(5) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. This disclosure is a prerequisite to any substantial acquisition crossing regulatory thresholds in shareholding. Asian Hotels (East) Limited is a heritage hospitality asset operator in Kolkata, listed on NSE and BSE. The filing does not explicitly state the acquisition quantum, but the regulatory trigger indicates movement across a material shareholding threshold.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 10(5)
framework.note: Disclosure requirement for acquirers when shareholding crosses thresholds; triggers mandatory general offer if threshold (25% or above) is breached.
Definition of 'acquirer' and 'substantial acquisition'; sets the scope of parties and transactions subject to the Code.
General offer requirements and exemptions (creeping acquisition, open market purchases); key to structuring the transaction.
Public announcement of the general offer and disclosure of acquirer's intention and financial details.
Director appointment rules; post-takeover governance implications if acquirer appoints board nominees.
Continuous disclosure obligations for listed companies; Asian Hotels (East) must report concert party formation and acquirer details.
Exemptions and conditions for concert party arrangements and related party acquisitions.

conditions: Disclosure under Reg. 10(5) filed with NSE
Potential general offer trigger if shareholding crosses 25% threshold
Creeping acquisition exemption may apply if purchases are within specified quarterly limits
approvals: Potential DCA (Panel for Takeovers and Mergers) clearance if general offer required
CCI clearance if acquisition triggers competition scrutiny (unlikely for single-company acquisition absent change-of-control)
structure.novel: Filing under Reg. 10(5) for an unnamed acquisition quantum suggests acquirer may be building stake in tranches below mandatory offer threshold or structuring under creeping exemption.

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
triggers.note: Disclosure of substantial shareholding crossing regulatory thresholds; mandatory if >2% (intimation), >5% (disclosure), >25% (general offer).
Continuous disclosure of concert party formation, shareholding changes >1%, and acquirer details.

firms.note: No law firm counsel identified in primary disclosure; typical practice would involve SEBI takeover counsel.
